items.author: fluffycrypt
items.context: Fluffy (157K seguidores), con un video de 46 s: "Este millonario cripto filtró la frase semilla de su wallet durante un livestream. Sus espectadores le robaron $2,5M en segundos". La cifra y el caso son lo que afirma el post; no están verificados.
items.suggested_text:
A seed phrase isn't a password you can reset; it is the wallet. Whoever sees those 12 or 24 words has exactly the same authority as the owner, and a sweep script can move everything before anyone realizes what happened. No support line, no chargeback.

That's why the core rule of self-custody is that the words never touch anything with a camera, a screen or an internet connection: not a photo, not a notes app, not a stream. A hardware wallet protects the signing, but it can't protect a phrase that has already been shown.

Most losses like this aren't a failure of Bitcoin's cryptography. They're a failure of the few seconds when the secret leaves the paper.
